title: Field-to-Scope QuickMap + Cost Deck for Enterprise Requests
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Sales and CS frequently hand off inbound enterprise feature asks that need an immediate, consistent, and lightweight scoping artifact to (a) set expectations with the customer and (b) allow PM/Eng to do a fast prioritization pass. Current handoffs are inconsistent: some are long email threads, others are single-line Slack messages. That causes delays and repeated clarification cycles.

Objective: Create a "QuickMap" template and an accompanying automated 'Cost Deck' (one-sheet) that frontline Sales/CS can fill in under 10 minutes. The artifact should produce: a 1-paragraph problem statement, high-level implementation risk band (Low/Medium/High), rough dev effort range (S/M/L), potential infra/security blockers, estimated unit cost/ops impact, and 3 recommended next steps (proof-of-concept, partner pilot, or backlog).

Why now: Increasing volume of enterprise asks (esp. private/VPC requests and Dedicated capacity changes) is slowing response times and creating churn in scoping meetings. A lean artifact will accelerate first-pass prioritization, improve handoff quality to Eng, and reduce meeting time by ~30%.
acceptance_criteria:
- Template available as Google Form + fillable doc in Drive
- Template auto-renders a 1-page 'Cost Deck' PDF with fields populated
- CS/Sales can complete in <= 10 minutes in pilot sessions
- PM triage can make a prioritization decision (Backlog/Planned/Requires Deep Scope) based on the Cost Deck without an immediate follow-up call in >= 60% of pilot cases
- Pilot with 6 accounts across Sales and CS completed and feedback logged
- Hand-off checklist includes pointers to security questions, sample contracts, and required logs/audit artifacts
scope:
In scope:
- Design and publish a lightweight QuickMap template for Sales/CS
- Implement a Google Form and a script that produces a rendered PDF Cost Deck
- Create PM rubric that maps QuickMap answers into triage buckets and effort estimates
- Run a 2-week pilot with 6 sales/CS reps and 6 customer requests
- Capture feedback and iterate on template

Out of scope:
- Full engineering estimates beyond rough S/M/L ranges
- Automated billing/econ modeling integration with internal finance systems
- New console UI; this is an interim lightweight operational artifact
solution_sketch:
1) Template fields: customer brief, use-case category (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), data sensitivity level, desired timeline, example traffic load, integrations required (S3/DB/KMS), success criteria, commercial ask (SLA/custom pricing), and security notes.
2) Decision rubric: map data sensitivity and integrations to security blockers; map timeline + traffic to infra complexity; map feature novelty to engineering risk. Each axis produces a Low/Medium/High band and a S/M/L dev range.
3) Cost Deck generation: Google Form triggers Apps Script that formats answers into a one-page drive document and exports PDF; include a small cost proxy table (token throughput assumptions, reserved GPU days estimate).
4) Enable quick flags: "Requires enterprise legal review", "Needs dedicated infra", "Possible workaround via hosted API".

Notes on accuracy: This is intentionally conservative and designed for prioritization only. Detailed scoping remains an engineer-driven activity after triage.
rollout_plan:
Week 0: Draft template and rubric (PM + Solutions Engineering)
Week 1: Build Form + Apps Script + Generate sample Cost Decks from 3 historic requests
Week 2: Pilot with 6 requests (2 Sales-led, 2 CS-managed, 2 partner referrals)
End of Week 2: Collect feedback, revise template
Week 3: Publish Template in Sales/CS playbook, run 45-min office hours for reps
Week 4: Iterate and hand off to Operations owner for ongoing maintenance
metrics:
- Time to first structured scope (minutes) for incoming enterprise asks (target < 60 minutes)
- % of triage decisions made without follow-up call (target >= 60%)
- Pilot satisfaction score from Sales/CS (target >= 4/5)
- Reduction in engineering kickoff clarification threads (target 30% fewer Slack threads per request)

decision_rationale: We opt for a lightweight operational artifact rather than a heavy UI integration because speed of adoption and low friction for Sales/CS are higher priority. The QuickMap + Cost Deck can be iterated rapidly and provides immediate value while engineering capacity is scheduled for deeper scoping when needed.
